raw_response:
I have been working this land since I was a young woman. My mother taught me, and her mother taught her. I don't need to read books — I know this soil, I know this weather, I know what my neighbors do and what works.

My 12 mu I split the way I always have: 8 mu for the wheat-maize rotation, and 4 mu for cotton. The cotton gives me cash to buy things. The wheat and maize feed my family and I sell what's left.

For the wheat, I'll put it in around Cold Dew festival in October like every year, after I finish picking cotton. I'll rotary-till the maize stubble first. I use the improved variety the village supply station sells — not the old seeds, but nothing too fancy either. I apply base fertilizer before planting and topdress in spring when the plants are jointing. I water three times: once before planting to wet the soil good, once in spring jointing, once at heading. Two pesticide sprays — one for aphids in spring, one for rust.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant maize right away. No need to plough again. My son can come back to help me broadcast the seeds. I use the hybrid everyone around here uses —郑单958 or whatever the station has. Two waterings if it doesn't rain enough. One pesticide spray.

The cotton I'll plough deep in March before planting. Cotton needs more water and more spraying — I'll irrigate four times and spray five times for bollworm and aphids. My daughter-in-law helps me pick in autumn. It's hard work but the price is decent.
